newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 13.52 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields fall to 13.52 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs fell 168 basis points to 13.52 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 50 billion bolivars of 180- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 15.20 percent coupon for a price of 100.79 percent. At last week's auction, the six-month notes yielded 15.20 percent.

The bank also sold 10 billion bolivars of 269-day notes with a 15.48 percent coupon at a price of 100.28 percent, and 10 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 15.77 percent coupon at an average price of 99.77 percent.
Yields for these notes fell 161 basis points to 15.06 percent for the 269-day bills, and 183 basis points to 16.04 percent for the 358-day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
